messages:
maya: Quick question — kotlin client + OkHttp streaming keeps dropping after ~5m idle with java.io.EOFException. We set readTimeout(0) and callTimeout(0) but still see disconnects. Anyone hit this?
jonathan: Often a proxy (nginx/GCLB) is closing idle connections. OkHttp timeouts stop client-side timeouts but won't prevent network-level idle drops. Check proxy_read_timeout / backend idle settings.
taylor: For http/2 you can use .pingInterval(Duration.ofSeconds(30)) on OkHttp to keep the connection alive. For http/1 chunked streams, server-side heartbeats are the most reliable.
maya: We're on GCLB + nginx sidecar, forgot about proxy timeouts. Is there a client-only tactic if changing infra is slow?
ash: (alias ash) Client-only hacks are limited. You can try periodic tiny requests to keep pool active or use a short reconnect/backoff in the reader. But better to config the proxy if possible.
ash: Also check you're not accidentally buffering the stream on the client — e.g., Gson's JsonReader can attempt to read more than one top-level value and block.
maya: We're actually using Jackson for binding but project pulled in an older Gson from another dep. Could shading cause weird buffering/compat issues?
jonathan: Yes. Mixed JSON libs can be subtle. For shading, prefer Gradle Shadow plugin with relocate rules, e.g.:
```
shadowJar {
  relocate 'com.google.gson', 'com.redwood.shaded.gson'
}
```
That avoids runtime clashes.
taylor: Also ensure Jackson modules (databind/core/annotations) are the same version — NoSuchMethodError usually means version skew.
meredith: I just pushed a small client change that sets readTimeout=0 and callTimeout=0 and tweaks ConnectionPool for long-lived streams — branch `1799901870`. @maya can you validate against your infra? :eyes: 
maya: Trying `1799901870` now. Getting NoSuchMethodError: com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.ObjectMapper.registerModule — smells like mixed jackson versions due to transitive deps.
ash: Run `./gradlew dependencyInsight --configuration runtimeClasspath --dependency jackson-databind` to find who pulls the old version. Exclude old transitive deps or align with constraints in the root build.
dev-bot: CI for branch 1799901870: integration tests ✅, shading tests ❌ (see artifacts).
maya: OK will run dependencyInsight and try exclusions + relocate for gson. If still failing I’ll ask infra to pin versions. Thanks all :thumbsup:
jonathan: If you want, paste your `build.gradle.kts` snippet and we can suggest exact exclusions/constraints. Quick tip: use `implementation('com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-databind:2.14.3') { force = true }` in the module that runs tests for a fast patch.
maya: Will do, pinging when I have the snippet. Appreciate the help!
